notes: Nineteen lists read. oecd.org returned 403, so OECD Safety indicators come from the public Better Life Index mirror (oecd-better-life-index.truth-and-beauty.net). The Ipsos PDF and Pew topline were read with a local PDF text extractor; Gallup tables were read from the page HTML. Wikidata QIDs came from the wbsearchentities API (22 lookups, not counted as searches). Coverage is low on most lists because nine candidates are waiting for review; once accepted, most lists pass 90%. Remaining gaps are outOfScope or broader on purpose: work safety (work sweep proposes unsafe-work), drinking water (home sweep proposes tap-water), suicide (mind sweep proposes suicidal-thoughts), politics as a safety risk (government sweep proposes political-violence), falls and drowning (personal injury; the founder pool lead 'I worry about what would happen if I fell or had an emergency while alone' could become a Body or Home pain), and pandemics (SDG 3.d, Health group). Likely twins for review: terrorism vs government/political-violence; school-shootings overlaps gun-violence and could sit under Kids; violence-against-women overlaps unsafe-at-home (personal) as the societal view; elder-abuse overlaps older-people-alone. CDC FastStats figures are the latest year shown on the page; the year isn't quoted, so prevalence says 'the latest year of CDC data'. child-abuse was removed from this run's candidates at the coordinator's request because the kids sweep 20261019-230115 proposes the same ID; its 4 list entries are marked outOfScope. Sources it relied on: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/child-maltreatment ("One in 5 women and 1 in 7 men report having been sexually abused as a child.", accessed 2026-10-19); https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/child-maltreatment ("Six in 10 children – or 400 million children – under 5 years of age regularly suffer physical punishment", accessed 2026-10-19). Prevalence as drafted: 1 in 5 women and 1 in 7 men report having been sexually abused as a child; 400 million children under 5 regularly suffer physical punishment or psychological violence at home (WHO).
